newsitem.title: IRAQ: U.S.-backed Kurds prepare to evacute N. Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-backed Kurds prepare to evacute N. Iraq.

text.p: Hundreds of Kurds who worked for the United States in northern Iraq prepared to evacute to Turkey on Sunday after a Baghdad-backed Kurdish faction took control of most of the region.

Witnesses said six battered blue-and-white buses, guarded by Iraqi Kurdish guerrillas, brought the Kurds to the Habur border crossing for passage to a camp inside Turkey where they were to be processed for asylum in the United States.

As many as 2,500 Iraqi Kurds were expected to be taken to a camp in the Turkish town of Silopi. Most worked as employees of U.S. aid programmes and the U.S.-led air operation patrolling a no-fly zone in northern Iraq.
Some of the Kurds are believed to have been engaged in intelligence activities for the Americans.
"I feel great. I just want to get across that bridge," said a refugee who identified himself only as Moyyad. A Turkish tank waited on the other side of the border.

The Kurds had been holed up in small hotels and private residences waiting to flee since Iraqi troops helped the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) faction take the city of Arbil from a rival group late last month.
Officials of the KDP, which now controls virtually all of northern Iraq, are reluctant to see so many of the region's skilled people leave and have played down the need for the departures.
